Generated Narrative: StructureDefinition Interaction

NameFlagsCard.TypeDescription & Constraints
Interaction 0..*BaseInteraction
identifier 0..*IdentifierUnique identifier(s) for this interaction definition.
name 1..1stringA short human-readable label for the interaction (e.g., 'Patient Demographics Query').
title 0..1stringA display title for the interaction.
description 0..1markdownA human-readable description of what this interaction accomplishes.
type 1..1codeThe type of actors involved.
Binding: Interaction Type (required)
status 0..1codeThe publication status of this interaction definition.
Binding: PublicationStatus (required)
date 0..1dateTimeThe date this interaction definition was last changed.
purpose 0..1markdownWhy this interaction is defined — the business or clinical need it addresses.
initiator 1..1Reference(ActorDefinition)The actor that triggers the interaction (logical source).
responder 1..1Reference(ActorDefinition)The actor that receives and responds to the interaction (logical endpoint).
participant 0..*BackboneElementAdditional actors involved in the interaction beyond initiator and responder.
actor 1..1Reference(ActorDefinition)The participant actor.
role 1..1codeThe role this participant plays in the interaction.
Binding: Participant Role (extensible)
position 0..1integerOrder in a sequential chain of intermediaries (1-based). Used when multiple participants form an ordered path between initiator and responder.
description 0..1stringWhat this participant does in the context of this specific interaction.
trigger 0..1stringA description of the event or condition that initiates this interaction.
preCondition 0..*stringConditions that must be true before this interaction can occur.
postCondition 0..*stringConditions that are expected to be true after this interaction completes successfully.
request 1..1BackboneElementThe outbound payload — what the initiator supplies.
description 0..1markdownA human-readable description of the request — the semantics of what is supplied, including what a human actor is expected to enter.
response 0..1BackboneElementThe return payload — what the responder returns. Absent for fire-and-forget patterns.
description 0..1markdownA human-readable description of the response — the semantics of what is returned.
semantics 0..1BackboneElementThe processing semantics of the interaction — what actors do during the exchange, beyond what is expressed in pre/postConditions and the payload structure.
description 0..1markdownOverall narrative description of the processing semantics.
actorBehavior 0..*BackboneElementThe expected behavior of a specific actor during this interaction.
actor 1..1Reference(ActorDefinition)The actor whose behavior is described.
expectation 1..1markdownWhat this actor is expected to do during the interaction (e.g., validate, cross-reference, transform, store, forward).

description:
A logical model representing an exchange between actors. 
This is the base model for all interactions, including user-to-system, system-to-user, 
system-to-system, and user-to-user exchanges. The Transaction logical model extends 
this for system-to-system technical contracts.

A logical model representing an exchange between actors. 
This is the base model for all interactions, including user-to-system, system-to-user, 
system-to-system, and user-to-user exchanges. The Transaction logical model extends 
this for system-to-system technical contracts.

May be used to represent additional information that is not part of the basic definition of the element and that modifies the understanding of the element in which it is contained and/or the understanding of the containing element's descendants. Usually modifier elements provide negation or qualification. To make the use of extensions safe and manageable, there is a strict set of governance applied to the definition and use of extensions. Though any implementer can define an extension, there is a set of requirements that SHALL be met as part of the definition of the extension. Applications processing a resource are required to check for modifier extensions.

Modifier extensions SHALL NOT change the meaning of any elements on Resource or DomainResource (including cannot change the meaning of modifierExtension itself).
element.comment: There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions.  The use of extensions is what allows the FHIR specification to retain a core level of simplicity for everyone.
element.requirements: Modifier extensions allow for extensions that *cannot* be safely ignored to be clearly distinguished from the vast majority of extensions which can be safely ignored.  This promotes interoperability by eliminating the need for implementers to prohibit the presence of extensions. For further information, see the [definition of modifier extensions](http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/extensibility.html#modifierExtension).

element.short: Interaction
element.definition:
A logical model representing an exchange between actors. 
This is the base model for all interactions, including user-to-system, system-to-user, 
system-to-system, and user-to-user exchanges. The Transaction logical model extends 
this for system-to-system technical contracts.
